iitjam-2025-01.title: Estimate the terms
iitjam-2025-01.body:
The series alternates with decreasing terms: $n=1$: $\frac{\pi^3}{16}\approx1.938$; $n=2$: $\frac{\pi^5}{768}\approx0.398$; $n=3$: $\frac{\pi^7}{92160}\approx0.033$. Partial sums $1.938,\ 1.540,\ 1.573,\dots$ settle near $1.571=\frac\pi2$; the other options are negative or $0.785$.

**Answer: (C)**

iitjam-2025-02.title: Exactness test
iitjam-2025-02.body:
Exactness needs $N_x=M_y=e^x\cos y-2\sin x$.

- (A) $N_x=e^x\sin y-2\sin x$ ✗
- (B) $N_x=e^x\cos y-2\sin x$ ✓
- (C) $N_x=e^x\cos y+2\cos x$ ✗
- (D) $N_x=e^x\sin y+2\cos x$ ✗

Indeed $d(e^x\sin y+2y\cos x)=(e^x\sin y-2y\sin x)dx+(e^x\cos y+2\cos x)dy$.

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-03.title: Difference quotients
iitjam-2025-03.body:
- $\dfrac{f(x)-f(0)}{x}=|x|\left|\sin\frac1x\right|$, and $0\le|x||\sin\frac1x|\le|x|\to0$. So $f'(0)=0$.
- $\dfrac{g(x)-g(0)}{x}=x\sin\frac1x+\cos\frac1x$. The first term $\to0$, but $\cos\frac1x$ has no limit (it equals $1$ at $x=\frac1{2k\pi}$ and $-1$ at $x=\frac1{(2k+1)\pi}$). So $g$ is not differentiable at 0.

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-04.title: Squeeze and sequences
iitjam-2025-04.body:
- $|f(x)|\le|x|^{1/8}\to0=f(0)$: $f$ is continuous at 0.
- Along $x_k=\frac{1}{(2k+1)\pi}\to0$: $g(x_k)=-e^{x_k}\to-1\ne1=g(0)$. So $g$ is not continuous at 0.

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-05.title: Double root
iitjam-2025-05.body:
$r^2-8r+16=(r-4)^2$: homogeneous solutions $e^{4x},\ xe^{4x}$ (this rules out (C), (D)).

Try $y_p=Ax^2e^{4x}$. Writing $y=u e^{4x}$, the operator becomes $(D-4)^2(ue^{4x})=u''e^{4x}$, so $u''=2$ gives $u=x^2$, i.e. $A=1$.

General solution: $\alpha_1e^{4x}+\alpha_2xe^{4x}+x^2e^{4x}$.

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-06.title: Determinant
iitjam-2025-06.body:
The matrix of $T$ is $\begin{pmatrix}1&0&1\\2&3&5\\0&2&2\end{pmatrix}$, with determinant $1(6-10)-0+1(4-0)=0$. A linear map $\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ with zero determinant is neither one-one nor onto.

Explicitly, $(1,1,-1)\mapsto(0,0,0)$.

**Answer: (D)**

iitjam-2025-07.title: Find $x$, then an eigenvector
iitjam-2025-07.body:
Expanding along the second column, $\det M=1\cdot\det\begin{pmatrix}2&-1\\2&x\end{pmatrix}=2x+2$. Eigenvalue 0 means $\det M=0$, so $x=-1$.

Then $M\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}2-1\\4-4\\2-1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}$: an eigenvector with eigenvalue 1. Hence $(M^4+M)v=(1+1)v=\begin{pmatrix}2\\0\\2\end{pmatrix}$.

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-08.title: Upper triangular matrix
iitjam-2025-08.body:
$T(1)=1$, $T(x)=1+x$, $T(x^2)=1+2x+x^2$, so
$$M=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&1\\0&1&2\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}.$$
It is upper triangular with diagonal $1,1,1$: $\det M=1$, rank 3, nullity 0, and the only eigenvalue is 1.

**Answer: (C)**

iitjam-2025-09.title: Cubing is an automorphism
iitjam-2025-09.body:
In an abelian group $\phi(x)=x^3$ is a homomorphism. Its kernel consists of elements with $x^3=e$; their order divides $\gcd(3,10)=1$, so the kernel is trivial and $\phi$ is a bijection of the finite group $G$. Hence exactly one $x$ satisfies $x^3=x_0$ (namely $x=x_0$ itself, since $x_0^3=x_0^2x_0=x_0$).

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-09.title: Cyclic model
iitjam-2025-09.body:
An abelian group of order 10 is $\mathbb Z_{10}$ (written additively). The element of order 2 is $5$, and $3x\equiv5\pmod{10}$ has the unique solution $x\equiv5$ because 3 is invertible mod 10 ($3\cdot7\equiv1$).

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-10.title: Change the order of integration
iitjam-2025-10.body:
The region is $0\le y\le1$, $\sqrt y\le x\le1$, i.e. $0\le x\le1$, $0\le y\le x^2$. So
$$\int_0^1\int_0^{x^2}3e^{x^3}\,dy\,dx=\int_0^13x^2e^{x^3}\,dx=\Big[e^{x^3}\Big]_0^1=e-1.$$

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-11.title: Orthogonal trajectories
iitjam-2025-11.body:
Differentiating $yx^2=\lambda$: $y'x^2+2xy=0$, so $y'=-\frac{2y}{x}$. Orthogonal curves satisfy $y'=\frac{x}{2y}$, i.e. $2y\,dy=x\,dx$, so $y^2=\frac{x^2}{2}+C$, or $x^2-2y^2=c$.

Through $(2,1)$: $c=4-2=2$. So the curve is $x^2-2y^2=2$.

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-11.title: Test each candidate
iitjam-2025-11.body:
All four curves pass through $(2,1)$, so the question is which one satisfies the orthogonal-trajectory equation $y'=\frac{x}{2y}$ at every point.

- (A) $y'=\frac x2$, while $\frac{x}{2y}=\frac{2}{x}$ on this curve: equal only at $x=2$ ✗.
- (B) $2x-4yy'=0\Rightarrow y'=\frac{x}{2y}$ everywhere ✓.
- (C) $y'=1\ne\frac{x}{2y}=\frac{x}{2(x-1)}$ in general ✗.
- (D) $y'=\frac1y$, which equals $\frac{x}{2y}$ only when $x=2$ ✗.

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-12.title: Homogeneous substitution
iitjam-2025-12.body:
The equation is $y'=\frac yx\ln\frac yx$. Put $y=vx$: $v+xv'=v\ln v$, so
$$\frac{dv}{v(\ln v-1)}=\frac{dx}{x}\implies\ln|\ln v-1|=\ln x+C\implies\ln v-1=Kx.$$
At $x=1$, $v=e^2$: $K=1$. So $\ln\frac yx=1+x$, i.e. $\varphi(x)=xe^{1+x}$, and $\varphi(2)=2e^3$.

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-13.title: Count by cycle type
iitjam-2025-13.body:
$S_4$ has: identity (1), transpositions (6), double transpositions (3), 3-cycles (8), 4-cycles (6).

- $x^3=id$ iff the order divides 3: identity and 3-cycles, $m=1+8=9$ (odd).
- $x^2\ne id$ iff the order is not 1 or 2: 3-cycles and 4-cycles, $n=8+6=14$ (even).

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-14.title: Solve explicitly
iitjam-2025-14.body:
Partial fractions: $\frac{1}{(y-1)(y-3)}=\frac12\left(\frac1{y-3}-\frac1{y-1}\right)$, so $\frac12\ln\left|\frac{y-3}{y-1}\right|=x+C$. At $x=0$, $y=2$: $C=0$. Since $\frac{y-3}{y-1}=-1<0$ initially,
$$\frac{y-3}{y-1}=-e^{2x}\implies\varphi(x)=\frac{3+e^{2x}}{1+e^{2x}}.$$
- $x\to\infty$: $\varphi\to1$ (A false).
- $x=\ln\sqrt2$: $e^{2x}=2$, $\varphi=\frac53$ (B false).
- $x\to-\infty$: $\varphi\to3$ (C true).
- $x=\ln\frac1{\sqrt2}$: $e^{2x}=\frac12$, $\varphi=\frac73$ (D false).

**Answer: (C)**

iitjam-2025-14.title: Phase line
iitjam-2025-14.body:
For $1<y<3$, $y'<0$, so the solution starting at 2 stays between the equilibria 1 and 3, decreasing: $\varphi(x)\to1$ as $x\to\infty$ and $\varphi(x)\to3$ as $x\to-\infty$. Since $1<\varphi<3$ everywhere, (B) and (D) (limits 1 and 6 at finite points, where $\varphi$ is continuous) are impossible.

**Answer: (C)**

iitjam-2025-15.title: Row reduce
iitjam-2025-15.body:
Look at the $3\times3$ minor from columns 1, 2, 3:
$$\det\begin{pmatrix}6&2&-6\\5&3&-9\\3&1&-2\end{pmatrix}=6(-6+9)-2(-10+27)-6(5-9)=18-34+24=8\ne0.$$
So $\operatorname{rank}M=3$. A $3\times4$ matrix of rank 3 has column space $\mathbb R^3$, so $Mx=b$ is solvable for every right-hand side $b$, in particular for $(8,16,32)^T$.

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-16.title: Block structure
iitjam-2025-16.body:
Expanding along the first row, $\det(M-\lambda I)=(-2-\lambda)\det\begin{pmatrix}2-\lambda&3\\-1&x-\lambda\end{pmatrix}$. For 3 to be an eigenvalue: $(2-3)(x-3)+3=0$, so $x=6$. The $2\times2$ block then has trace 8 and determinant 15, so the eigenvalues of $M$ are $-2,3,5$.

Consistency check: $M(0,1,1)^T=(0,\ 5,\ -1+6)^T=5(0,1,1)^T$, so $M^3(0,1,1)^T=125(0,1,1)^T$ ✓.

$M^2+M=M(M+I)$ has eigenvalues $\lambda(\lambda+1)$: $2,\ 12,\ 30$, all nonzero, so it is invertible. And $x=6\ne5$.

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-17.title: Strict convexity
iitjam-2025-17.body:
$f''(x)=20+e^x+4\sin2x+\cos x\ge20-4-1>0$. So $f'$ is strictly increasing. Also $f'(x)=20x+e^x-2\cos2x+\sin x\to\pm\infty$ as $x\to\pm\infty$, so $f'$ has exactly one zero, where $f$ has its unique local (and global) minimum.

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-18.title: Terms do not tend to zero
iitjam-2025-18.body:
- $|x_n|=\cos\frac1n\to1$, so $x_n\not\to0$ and $\sum x_n$ diverges.
- $y_n\ge n\cdot\frac{1}{2n}=\frac12$ for all $n$ (in fact $y_n\to\ln2$), so $y_n\not\to0$ and $\sum y_n$ diverges.

**Answer: (D)**

iitjam-2025-19.title: Induction between the fixed points
iitjam-2025-19.body:
$x_{n+1}-x_n=\frac{x_n^2-5x_n+6}{5}=\frac{(x_n-2)(x_n-3)}{5}$, and $g(x)=\frac{x^2+6}{5}$ is increasing on $[2,3]$ with $g(2)=2$, $g(3)=3$.

By induction $2<x_n<3$ for all $n$ (true for $x_1=2.5$; if $2<x_n<3$ then $2=g(2)<g(x_n)<g(3)=3$). Then $(x_n-2)(x_n-3)<0$, so $x_{n+1}<x_n$. The sequence is decreasing and bounded (it converges to 2).

**Answer: (D)**

iitjam-2025-20.title: Contraction
iitjam-2025-20.body:
Clearly $x_n\ge2$ for all $n$ (since $x_{n+1}=2+\frac1{2x_n}>2$).

- $x_nx_{n+1}=2x_n+\frac12\ge4.5>4$, so $x_{n+1}\ge\frac4{x_n}$ for all $n$.
- $|x_{n+1}-x_n|=\left|\frac1{2x_n}-\frac1{2x_{n-1}}\right|=\frac{|x_n-x_{n-1}|}{2x_nx_{n-1}}\le\frac18|x_n-x_{n-1}|$. A sequence whose successive differences shrink geometrically is Cauchy (the tail sums $\sum|x_{k+1}-x_k|$ are bounded by a convergent geometric series).

(The limit is $1+\frac{\sqrt6}{2}$.)

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-21.title: Growth rates
iitjam-2025-21.body:
- $|x_n|=\frac{3^n}{n^3}\to\infty$, so every subsequence is unbounded: none converges.
- $y_n=4\left(1+(-1)^n(3/4)^n\right)^{1/n}$. The bracket lies in $[\frac14,\frac74]$ and $c^{1/n}\to1$ for constants $c>0$, so $y_n\to4$. In particular $(y_n)$ itself is a convergent subsequence.

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-22.title: Permutation matrix
iitjam-2025-22.body:
The columns of $M_\sigma$ are columns 2, 3, 1 of $M$, so $M_\sigma=MP$ where $P$ is the permutation matrix of the 3-cycle $\sigma$. A 3-cycle is even, so $\det P=1$ and $\det M_\sigma=\det M$.

$M-M_\sigma=M(I-P)$ and $M$ is invertible, so the nullity equals that of $I-P$. $Pv=v$ means $v_{\sigma(j)}=v_j$ cyclically, i.e. $v_1=v_2=v_3$: the kernel of $I-P$ is spanned by $(1,1,1)^T$, so the nullity is 1.

**Answer: (C)**

iitjam-2025-23.title: Elements of order 3 and divisibility
iitjam-2025-23.body:
- A homomorphism $\mathbb Z_3\to\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ is determined by the image $t$ of $\bar1$, which must satisfy $3t=0$, i.e. $t\in\{0,\frac13,\frac23\}+\mathbb Z$. It is injective iff $t\ne0$: $m=2$.
- $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ is divisible: every element is $3s$ for some $s$. Under a homomorphism $\phi$ to $\mathbb Z_3$, $\phi(3s)=3\phi(s)=0$. So $\phi$ is trivial: $n=1$.

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-24.title: Kernels of functionals
iitjam-2025-24.body:
Each $f_i$ is a nonzero functional, so by rank–nullity $\dim\ker f_i=3$. From $\ker f_1\subseteq\ker f_2$ and equal dimensions, $\ker f_1=\ker f_2$; likewise $\ker f_1=\ker f_3$. Then $\ker T=\ker f_1\cap\ker f_2\cap\ker f_3=\ker f_1$, which has dimension 3.

**Answer: (C)**

iitjam-2025-25.title: Ratio test
iitjam-2025-25.body:
All $x_n>0$, and $\dfrac{x_{n+1}}{x_n}=\frac12+\frac{\sin^2n}{n}\le\frac12+\frac1n\le\frac34$ for $n\ge4$. So $x_n\le x_4(3/4)^{n-4}$ for $n\ge4$ and $\sum x_n$ converges by comparison with a geometric series. Then $x_n\to0$, so $x_n^2\le x_n$ and $x_nx_{n+1}\le x_n$ eventually, and those series converge too. Only (A) is true.

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-26.title: Telescoping
iitjam-2025-26.body:
Since $x_{k+1}-x_k=4$: $\frac{1}{x_kx_{k+1}}=\frac14\left(\frac1{x_k}-\frac1{x_{k+1}}\right)$. So
$$\sum_{k=2}^{n+1}\frac{1}{x_kx_{k+1}}=\frac14\left(\frac1{x_2}-\frac1{x_{n+2}}\right)\to\frac1{4x_2}$$
because $x_n\to\infty$. Then $\frac{1}{4x_2}=\frac1{24}$ gives $x_2=6$ and $x_1=2$.

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-27.title: Critical points
iitjam-2025-27.body:
$f_x=2xe^y$, $f_y=e^y(x^2+y^2+2y)$. Critical points: $x=0$ and $y^2+2y=0$, i.e. $(0,0)$ and $(0,-2)$.

- $(0,0)$: $f\ge0=f(0,0)$, a (global) minimum.
- $(0,-2)$: $f_{xx}=2e^y=2e^{-2}$, $f_{xy}=2xe^y=0$, $f_{yy}=e^y(x^2+y^2+4y+2)=e^{-2}(4-8+2)=-2e^{-2}$. The Hessian determinant is negative: a saddle point.

So exactly one local minimum and no local maximum.

**Answer: (C)**

iitjam-2025-28.title: Cylindrical coordinates
iitjam-2025-28.body:
$\Omega$ is the part of $\{x^2+y^2\le z\le4\}$ with $x,y\ge0$: a quarter of the region between the paraboloid and the plane, over the quarter disc $r\le2$, $0\le\theta\le\frac\pi2$.
$$V=\int_0^{\pi/2}\int_0^2(4-r^2)\,r\,dr\,d\theta=\frac\pi2\left[2r^2-\frac{r^4}{4}\right]_0^2=\frac\pi2\cdot4=2\pi.$$

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-28.title: Slices in $z$
iitjam-2025-28.body:
At height $z\in[0,4]$ the cross-section is a quarter disc of radius $\sqrt z$, area $\frac{\pi z}{4}$. So $V=\int_0^4\frac{\pi z}{4}dz=\frac\pi4\cdot8=2\pi$.

**Answer: (B)**

iitjam-2025-29.title: Convert to an ODE
iitjam-2025-29.body:
The right side is differentiable, so $\varphi$ is too: $\varphi'=\varphi+\cos x$, with $\varphi(0)=0$.

A particular solution $a\cos x+b\sin x$ needs $-a\sin x+b\cos x=a\cos x+b\sin x+\cos x$, so $b=-a$ and $b=a+1$: $a=-\frac12$, $b=\frac12$. With $\varphi(0)=0$:
$$\varphi(x)=\frac{e^x+\sin x-\cos x}{2}.$$
Then $2\varphi(x)-e^x=\sin x-\cos x\to1$ as $x\to\frac\pi2$.

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-29.title: Verify
iitjam-2025-29.body:
With $\varphi=\frac12(e^x+\sin x-\cos x)$: $\int_0^x\varphi=\frac12(e^x-1-\cos x+1-\sin x)=\frac12(e^x-\cos x-\sin x)$, and adding $\sin x$ gives $\frac12(e^x-\cos x+\sin x)=\varphi(x)$ ✓. The limit is $\sin\frac\pi2-\cos\frac\pi2=1$.

**Answer: (A)**

iitjam-2025-30.title: Monotone even function
iitjam-2025-30.body:
Let $h(x)=8x^2+x^4+x^8-\cos x$, an even function with $h(0)=-1<0$ and $h(1)=10-\cos1>0$. For $x>0$, $h'(x)=16x+4x^3+8x^7+\sin x>0$ (since $16x+\sin x>0$). So $h$ has exactly one positive zero, and by evenness exactly one negative zero; $x=0$ is not a zero. Total: 2.

**Answer: (C)**

iitjam-2025-31.title: Check each statement
iitjam-2025-31.body:
- **(A)** For fixed $x\ne0$: $\lim_{y\to0}f=\frac{0}{x^2}=0$, so the first iterated limit is 0. For fixed $y\ne0$: $\lim_{x\to0}f=\frac{y^5}{y^4}=y\to0$. Both exist ✓.
- **(B)/(C)** $f(x,0)=0$, so $f_x(0,0)=0$. $f(0,y)=y$, so $f_y(0,0)=1$. Both exist: (C) ✓, (B) ✗.
- **(D)** Along $x=y^2$: $f=\frac{y^4+y^5}{2y^4}=\frac{1+y}{2}\to\frac12\ne f(0,0)$. So $f$ is not even continuous at the origin, hence not differentiable ✓.

**Answer: A, C, D**

iitjam-2025-32.title: Use $w_x=\mu M$, $w_y=\mu N$
iitjam-2025-32.body:
The hypothesis says $w_x=\mu M$ and $w_y=\mu N$.

- **(A)** $\mu wM\,dx+\mu wN\,dy=w\,dw=d\left(\tfrac{w^2}{2}\right)$: exact ✓.
- **(B)** $\mu w^2M\,dx+\mu w^2N\,dy=w^2\,dw=d\left(\tfrac{w^3}{3}\right)$: exact ✓.
- **(C)** Integrate $dw$ along $(0,0)\to(x,0)\to(x,y)$: $w(x,0)-w(0,0)=\int_0^xw_x(s,0)ds$ and $w(x,y)-w(x,0)=\int_0^yw_y(x,t)dt$ ✓.
- **(D)** False in general: with $\mu=1$, $M=0$, $N=1$, $w=y$, the right side is $0+0+\int_0^x1\,dt=x\ne y$. (The correct formula along $(0,0)\to(0,y)\to(x,y)$ would have $\int_0^y$ in the second integral.)

**Answer: A, B, C**

iitjam-2025-33.title: Bernoulli substitution $v=\sqrt y$
iitjam-2025-33.body:
$v'=\frac{y'}{2\sqrt y}=\frac{2ye^x+2e^x\sqrt y}{2\sqrt y}=e^xv+e^x$. So $v'-e^xv=e^x$; with integrating factor $e^{-e^x}$:
$$\left(ve^{-e^x}\right)'=e^xe^{-e^x}\implies ve^{-e^x}=-e^{-e^x}+C\implies v=Ce^{e^x}-1.$$
$v(0)=1$: $Ce=2$, so $v=2e^{e^x-1}-1$ and
$$\varphi(x)=\left(2e^{e^x-1}-1\right)^2.$$
(On $(-1,\infty)$, $e^x-1>e^{-1}-1\approx-0.63$, so $v>2e^{-0.63}-1>0$.)

- (A) $\varphi\to\infty$ as $x\to\infty$ ✓.
- (B) At $x=\ln2$: $v=2e-1$, $\varphi=(2e-1)^2$ ✓; (C) ✗.
- (D) $v$ is positive and strictly increasing, so $\varphi=v^2$ is strictly increasing ✓.

**Answer: A, B, D**

iitjam-2025-34.title: Limit and differentiability
iitjam-2025-34.body:
- Since $\frac{y^2}{x^2+y^2}\le1$: $|f(x,y)|\le|x^2+\sin x|\to0$. The limit is 0: (B) ✓, (A) ✗.
- $f(x,0)=0$ and $f(0,y)=0$, so both partial derivatives at the origin are 0. Differentiability would require $\frac{f(x,y)}{\sqrt{x^2+y^2}}\to0$. In polar form, with $x=r\cos\theta$, $y=r\sin\theta$:
$$\frac{f}{r}=\frac{(r^2\cos^2\theta+\sin(r\cos\theta))\sin^2\theta}{r}\to\cos\theta\sin^2\theta,$$
which depends on $\theta$ (e.g. $\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}$ along $y=x$). So $f$ is not differentiable: (D) ✓, (C) ✗.

**Answer: B, D**

iitjam-2025-35.title: Determinant and explicit relations
iitjam-2025-35.body:
- **(A)** The matrix with rows $u_1,\dots,u_4$ is lower triangular in the first three columns; its determinant is $1\cdot2\cdot1\cdot1=2\ne0$. Independent ✓.
- **(B)** $(u_1-u_2)+(u_2-u_3)+(u_3-u_4)+(u_4-u_1)=0$: dependent ✓.
- **(C)** Changing signs of vectors does not affect independence, so this set is independent ✗.
- **(D)** $(u_1+u_2)-(u_2+u_3)+(u_3+u_4)-(u_4+u_1)=0$: dependent, so the statement is false ✗.

**Answer: A, B**

iitjam-2025-36.title: Squeeze
iitjam-2025-36.body:
For $1\le k\le n$: $\frac{k}{n^2+n}\le\frac{k}{n^2+k}\le\frac{k}{n^2}$. Summing:
$$\frac12=\frac{n(n+1)/2}{n^2+n}\le x_n\le\frac{n(n+1)}{2n^2}=\frac12+\frac1{2n}.$$
- (A) $x_n\to\frac12$ ✓.
- (B)/(C) $x_n\ge\frac12$, so $\sum x_n$ diverges: (C) ✓, (B) ✗.
- (D) For $n\ge2$, $x_n\le\frac12+\frac14=\frac34$, so $x_n^n\le(3/4)^n$ and $\sum x_n^n$ converges ✓.

**Answer: A, C, D**

iitjam-2025-37.title: Mean value theorem and Taylor
iitjam-2025-37.body:
- MVT: $f'(c)=\frac{f(1)-f(0)}{1}=-3$ for some $c\in(0,1)$, so $|f'(c)|=3>2$: (B) ✓, (A) ✗.
- Taylor with Lagrange remainder: $f(1)=f(0)+f'(0)+\frac{f''(\xi)}{2}$ for some $\xi\in(0,1)$, i.e. $-3=2+\frac{f''(\xi)}2$, so $f''(\xi)=-10$ and $|f''(\xi)|=10$: (D) ✓, (C) ✗.

(Example: $f(x)=2x-5x^2$ satisfies the conditions with $f''\equiv-10$.)

**Answer: B, D**

iitjam-2025-38.title: Mean value theorem on each interval
iitjam-2025-38.body:
MVT gives $c_1\in(0,1)$, $c_2\in(1,2)$, $c_3\in(2,3)$ with
$$f'(c_1)=-6,\qquad f'(c_2)=10,\qquad f'(c_3)=-6.$$
- (B) $|f'(c_1)|=6\ge5$ ✓, so (A) ✗.
- (C) $f'$ is continuous (it is differentiable) and changes sign between $c_1$ and $c_2$, so it vanishes there ✓.
- (D) $f'(c_1)=f'(c_3)$, so by Rolle's theorem applied to $f'$ there is $x_3\in(c_1,c_3)$ with $f''(x_3)=0$ ✓.

**Answer: B, C, D**

iitjam-2025-39.title: Find generators
iitjam-2025-39.body:
- $U(8)=\{1,3,5,7\}$: every element squares to 1, no element of order 4 — not cyclic.
- $U(5)=\{1,2,3,4\}$: $2$ has powers $2,4,3,1$ — cyclic ✓.
- $U(12)=\{1,5,7,11\}$: every element squares to 1 — not cyclic.
- $U(9)=\{1,2,4,5,7,8\}$: $2$ has powers $2,4,8,7,5,1$ — cyclic of order 6 ✓.

(In general $U(n)$ is cyclic iff $n=1,2,4,p^k,2p^k$ for an odd prime $p$.)

**Answer: B, D**

iitjam-2025-40.title: Union of subspaces
iitjam-2025-40.body:
A union of two subspaces is a subspace iff one contains the other. Here that means $V_i\subseteq V_1$.

$V_1$ is the plane with normal $(1,2,3)\times(1,1,0)=(-3,3,-1)$, i.e. $-3x+3y-z=0$. Test each spanning vector:
- $(1,-1,0)$: $-3-3-0=-6\ne0$ ✗
- $(1,1,1)$: $-3+3-1=-1\ne0$ ✗
- $(1,3,6)$: $-3+9-6=0$ ✓ (indeed $(1,3,6)=2(1,2,3)-(1,1,0)$)
- $(1,0,-3)$: $-3+0+3=0$ ✓ (indeed $(1,0,-3)=-(1,2,3)+2(1,1,0)$)

**Answer: C, D**

iitjam-2025-41.title: Root test
iitjam-2025-41.body:
The coefficients are $a_n=\frac{1}{(-2)^nn^2}$, and $|a_n|^{1/n}=\frac{1}{2\,n^{2/n}}\to\frac12$. By the Cauchy–Hadamard formula the radius is $R=2$.

**Answer: 2.00**

iitjam-2025-42.title: Standard limits
iitjam-2025-42.body:
With $h=\frac1{2n}\to0$: $8n=\frac4h$, so the expression is
$$4\cdot\frac{e^h-1}{h}\cdot(\sin h+|\cos h|)\to4\cdot1\cdot(0+1)=4.$$

**Answer: 4.00**

iitjam-2025-43.title: Series
iitjam-2025-43.body:
$1-\cos x=\frac{x^2}{2}+O(x^4)$ and $2^{2+x}-4=4(e^{x\ln2}-1)=4x\ln2+O(x^2)$. The product is $2x^3\ln2+O(x^4)$, so the limit is $2\ln2$ and $\alpha=2$.

**Answer: 2.00**

iitjam-2025-45.title: Surface area of a graph
iitjam-2025-45.body:
For $z=g(x,y)$, $dS=\sqrt{1+g_x^2+g_y^2}\,dA=\sqrt{1+1+1}\,dA=\sqrt3\,dA$. Over the unit disc (area $\pi$): $S=\sqrt3\pi$, so $(S/\pi)^2=3$.

**Answer: 3.00**

iitjam-2025-45.title: Projection angle
iitjam-2025-45.body:
The plane's unit normal is $\frac{(1,1,-1)}{\sqrt3}$, making angle $\gamma$ with the $z$-axis where $|\cos\gamma|=\frac1{\sqrt3}$. A planar region projects onto the $xy$-plane with area multiplied by $|\cos\gamma|$, so $S=\frac{\pi}{1/\sqrt3}=\sqrt3\pi$ and $(S/\pi)^2=3$.

**Answer: 3.00**

iitjam-2025-46.title: Rank of the coefficient matrix
iitjam-2025-46.body:
$V_1\cap V_2\cap V_3$ is the null space of
$$\begin{pmatrix}1&1&0&2\\0&2&1&1\\1&3&1&3\end{pmatrix}.$$
Row 3 = Row 1 + Row 2, and rows 1, 2 are independent, so the rank is 2 and the nullity is $4-2=2$.

**Answer: 2**

iitjam-2025-48.title: Area and centroid
iitjam-2025-48.body:
$\iint_T(5-y)=5\cdot\text{Area}-\bar y\cdot\text{Area}$. The area is $\frac12$ and the centroid has $\bar y=\frac{0+0+1}{3}=\frac13$. So the integral is $\frac12\left(5-\frac13\right)=\frac73$.

**Answer: 2.33**

iitjam-2025-49.title: Compute on monomials
iitjam-2025-49.body:
$T(x^k)=kx^k$, so $T$ is diagonal with eigenvalues $0,1,2,3,4$: $\ker T=\operatorname{span}\{1\}$ and the image of $T$ is spanned by $x,x^2,x^3,x^4$.

$S(x^k)=k(x+1)x^{k-1}$, which is nonzero for $k\ge1$, and $S$ restricted to $\operatorname{span}\{x,\dots,x^4\}$ is injective (the images $(x+1),\,2(x+1)x,\,3(x+1)x^2,\,4(x+1)x^3$ have distinct degrees).

So $S(T(p))=0\iff T(p)=0\iff p$ is constant. Nullity $=1$.

**Answer: 1**

iitjam-2025-51.title: Recognise a derivative
iitjam-2025-51.body:
Let $F(x)=\int_0^xf(t)dt$. Then $\frac{d}{dx}\big(\sin x\,F(x)\big)=\cos x\,F(x)+\sin x\,f(x)$, exactly the integrand. So the integral equals $\sin\frac\pi4\,F(\frac\pi4)-0=\frac{F(\pi/4)}{\sqrt2}$. Setting this equal to $\sqrt2$: $F(\frac\pi4)=2$.

**Answer: 2.00**

iitjam-2025-51.title: Integrate by parts
iitjam-2025-51.body:
$\int_0^{\pi/4}\cos x\,F(x)\,dx=\Big[\sin x\,F(x)\Big]_0^{\pi/4}-\int_0^{\pi/4}\sin x\,f(x)\,dx$. Adding $\int\sin x f(x)dx$ leaves $\frac{1}{\sqrt2}F(\frac\pi4)=\sqrt2$, so $\int_0^{\pi/4}f=2$.

**Answer: 2.00**

iitjam-2025-52.title: Orbit–stabiliser
iitjam-2025-52.body:
The set is the centraliser of $\sigma=(1\,2\,3)$. Its conjugacy class is the set of all 3-cycles in $S_4$, of size 8. So $|C(\sigma)|=\frac{24}{8}=3$.

**Answer: 3**

iitjam-2025-52.title: Direct description
iitjam-2025-52.body:
$\tau\sigma\tau^{-1}=(\tau(1)\,\tau(2)\,\tau(3))$. For this to equal $(1\,2\,3)$, $\tau$ must fix 4 and map $(1,2,3)$ to a cyclic rotation of $(1,2,3)$. That gives $\tau\in\{id,(1\,2\,3),(1\,3\,2)\}$: 3 elements.

**Answer: 3**

iitjam-2025-53.title: Use $f'(0)$
iitjam-2025-53.body:
$f(0)=0$ and $f'(0)=2-1=1$, so $\frac{f(x/i)}{x}\to\frac1i$ as $x\to0$. Hence the limit is
$$\sum_{i=1}^ki^2\cdot\frac1i=\sum_{i=1}^ki=\frac{k(k+1)}2.$$
$\frac{k(k+1)}{2}=45$ gives $k=9$.

**Answer: 9**

iitjam-2025-54.title: Differentiate the geometric series
iitjam-2025-54.body:
With $r=\left(\frac34\right)^2=\frac9{16}$, the series is $\sum_{n\ge1}nr^{n-1}=\frac{1}{(1-r)^2}$ (derivative of $\frac1{1-r}$). So the sum is $\frac{1}{(7/16)^2}=\frac{256}{49}\approx5.22$.

**Answer: 5.22**

iitjam-2025-55.title: Euler substitution $x=e^t$
iitjam-2025-55.body:
With $x=e^t$, $x\frac{dy}{dx}=\dot y$ and $x^2\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\ddot y-\dot y$. The equation becomes
$$\ddot y-2\dot y+y=6te^t.$$
The characteristic root 1 is double; a particular solution is $t^3e^t$ (writing $y=ue^t$ turns the left side into $\ddot ue^t$, and $\ddot u=6t$ gives $u=t^3$). So
$$\varphi=x\left(A+B\ln x+(\ln x)^3\right).$$
$\varphi(1)=A=-3$; $\varphi(e)=e(-3+B+1)=0\Rightarrow B=2$.

$\varphi'(x)=A+B\ln x+(\ln x)^3+B+3(\ln x)^2$, so $\varphi'(1)=A+B=-1$ and $|\varphi'(1)|=1$.

**Answer: 1.00**

iitjam-2025-56.title: Integrating factor
iitjam-2025-56.body:
Multiply by $e^{x^2}$: $\left(ye^{x^2}\right)'=(2+4x^2)e^{x^2}=\left(2xe^{x^2}\right)'$. So $ye^{x^2}=2xe^{x^2}+C$, and $\varphi(0)=0$ gives $C=0$. Hence $\varphi(x)=2x$ and $\varphi(2)=4$.

**Answer: 4.00**

iitjam-2025-56.title: Guess a polynomial
iitjam-2025-56.body:
Try $y=ax+b$: $a+2x(ax+b)=2+4x^2$ gives $a=2$, $b=0$. So $y=2x$ is a solution with $y(0)=0$, and by uniqueness $\varphi(x)=2x$, $\varphi(2)=4$.

**Answer: 4.00**

iitjam-2025-57.title: Integrate over the base triangle
iitjam-2025-57.body:
The lines $y=0$, $2y=x$ and $x=\frac12$ cut out the triangle $0\le x\le\frac12$, $0\le y\le\frac x2$ in the $xy$-plane (vertices $(0,0)$, $(\frac12,0)$, $(\frac12,\frac14)$). Over it the solid runs from $z=0$ up to the plane $z=4-2x-y$ (which is positive there).
$$V=\int_0^{1/2}\int_0^{x/2}(4-2x-y)\,dy\,dx=\int_0^{1/2}\left(2x-x^2-\frac{x^2}{8}\right)dx=\frac14-\frac98\cdot\frac1{24}=\frac{39}{192}.$$
So $64V=\frac{39}{3}=13$.

**Answer: 13.00**

iitjam-2025-57.title: Average height
iitjam-2025-57.body:
The base triangle has area $\frac12\cdot\frac12\cdot\frac14=\frac1{16}$ and centroid $\left(\frac13,\frac1{12}\right)$. Since the height $4-2x-y$ is linear, the volume is area times height at the centroid: $\frac1{16}\left(4-\frac23-\frac1{12}\right)=\frac1{16}\cdot\frac{39}{12}=\frac{39}{192}$. So $64V=13$.

**Answer: 13.00**

iitjam-2025-58.title: Compare coefficients
iitjam-2025-58.body:
For $p=\sum_{k=0}^3a_kx^k$: $xp'=\sum ka_kx^k$. The condition $xp'=3p$ means $(k-3)a_k=0$ for each $k$, so $a_0=a_1=a_2=0$ and $a_3$ is free. $H=\operatorname{span}\{x^3\}$, dimension 1.

**Answer: 1**

iitjam-2025-59.title: Cyclic group of order 35
iitjam-2025-59.body:
$G\cong\mathbb Z_5\times\mathbb Z_7\cong\mathbb Z_{35}$. A cyclic group has exactly $\varphi(d)$ elements of order $d$ for each divisor $d$. So $m=\varphi(5)=4$ and $n=\varphi(7)=6$, and $m+n=10$.

**Answer: 10**

iitjam-2025-60.title: Abelianisation
iitjam-2025-60.body:
$\mathbb Z_6$ is abelian, so any homomorphism $\phi:S_4\to\mathbb Z_6$ kills the commutator subgroup $[S_4,S_4]=A_4$. Hence $\phi$ factors through $S_4/A_4\cong\mathbb Z_2$ and its image has at most 2 elements. It cannot be onto $\mathbb Z_6$.

**Answer: 0**

iitjam-2025-60.title: Generators of order 2
iitjam-2025-60.body:
$S_4$ is generated by transpositions, which have order 2. Their images in $\mathbb Z_6$ lie in $\{0,3\}$, so the image of $S_4$ is contained in the subgroup $\{0,3\}$. No surjection exists.

**Answer: 0**
